chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aamir ibn Abdullah ibn Juz'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the soul reaches the throat, an angel comes to him and says to him: O you, or O so-and-so! As for what you were hoping for, then despair of it, and that is the return to the world; and as for what you were fearing, then you are secured from it.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the soul and the person's hopes and fears when death occurs?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the psychological transition at the moment of death, where the angel of death confirms the finality of the soul's departure. This event underscores the Shia concept of *Barzakh* as the immediate threshold where the potential for repentance ceases, and the reality of one's spiritual state becomes fixed.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from someone else, from AbanBin Usman, from Aamir Bin Abdullah Bin Juza’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the soul comes to be in the throat, an Angel comes over to him and says to him: ‘O you!’, or ‘O so and so! As for what you were hoping for, so despair from it’, and it is the returning to the world, ‘And as for what you were fearing, so you are (now) secured from it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Kindiy from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Judha‘ah who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘When a soul reaches the throat, an angel comes and says to him, “O you, - or so and so - what you had hoped for, be certain, is of no avail to you, meaning returning to the worldly life, but you have become safe from whatever you were afraid of.’””
